task_description: Write a method in Dafny to check whether a given string is a decimal number with a precision of 2.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method IsDecimalWithPrecision2(s: string) returns (result: bool)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The result is true if the string represents a decimal number with at most two digits after the decimal point
- The result is false if the string does not represent such a decimal number
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.
In this case:
    method IsDecimalWithPrecision2(s: string) returns (result: bool)
    
Step 2: Determine the preconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - There are no preconditions; the method can handle any string input.
    
Dafny specification:
    requires s != null
    
Step 3: Determine the postconditions.
In this case:
Natural language description:
    - The result is true if the input string represents a decimal number with at most two digits after the decimal point
- The result is false otherwise

Dafny specification:
    ensures result <==> IsValidDecimal(s)
where
    predicate IsValidDecimal(str: string)
      reads str
    {
        // Checks if str matches the pattern: optional sign, digits, optional decimal point with up to two digits
        // For simplicity, we can define a helper predicate to verify pattern
        str != "" &&
        ( // optional sign
          str[0] == '-' || str[0] == '+' || true
        ) &&
        // split on decimal point
        var parts := str.Split('.');
        parts.Length <= 2 &&
        (parts.Length == 1 || parts[1].Length <= 2) &&
        // all parts are digits
        (forall p in parts :: p != "" ==> AllDigits(p))
    }

    predicate AllDigits(s: string)
      reads s
    {
        (forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> '0' <= s[i] <= '9')
    }

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.
In this case:

```dafny
predicate AllDigits(s: string)
  reads s
{
    (forall i :: 0 <= i < |s| ==> '0' <= s[i] <= '9')
}

predicate IsValidDecimal(str: string)
  reads str
{
    str != "" &&
    (str[0] == '-' || str[0] == '+') || true
} &&
    var parts := str.Split('.');
    parts.Length <= 2 &&
    (parts.Length == 1 || parts[1].Length <= 2) &&
    (forall p in parts :: p != "" ==> AllDigits(p))
}

method IsDecimalWithPrecision2(s: string) returns (result: bool)
    requires s != null
    ensures result <==> IsValidDecimal(s)
{
    result := IsValidDecimal(s);
}
```
